input.conclusion: No — not without fresh owner approval. The currently-standing decision is the owner decision of 2026-09-05 that dropped Ubuntu and macOS from the verify matrix, followed by a second same-day decision explicitly declining to enable remote CI for macOS even on a scheduled lane. EPIC-105's earlier case for macOS on the PR gate is real but superseded. What the record does require is the honesty half, already delivered: while nothing measures macOS, no document may claim it is verified, and the README reads "not currently measured". The re-add is designed and costed (ROADMAP recommends option B, a nightly lane, ~3m47s) but blocked pending runner approval.
key_facts: EPIC-105 (commit 29e7fbd, PR #140, 2026-09-03) added macos-latest to the verify matrix and measured it green — 112 test files, 2,463 tests, the packaging suite (npm pack, global install, installed binary) and all seven signal tests passing in 3m47s — and argued macOS should stay on the pull-request gate.

That was reversed: commit 9bae9f2 (PR #155, 2026-09-05), 'ci: Windows is the only platform this workflow tests', records an owner decision dropping Ubuntu and macOS from verify and states that the workflow no longer measures macOS and no record should claim it does.

.github/workflows/ci.yml still carries the Windows-only matrix and that comment (lines 72-91); the file's most recent commit is 9100405 of 2026-09-05, so the reversal is the current state rather than an interim one.

A second owner decision on 2026-09-05 superseded the runner half of an earlier instruction to add scheduled macOS validation: 'do not enable remote CI for macOS', recorded as the owner's last priority (docs/EPICs/EPIC-115-macOS-Packaging-Validation.md).

EPIC-115 is CLOSED with coverage DEFERRED at P2 lowered by the owner; its validation record states no macOS runner was enabled by owner decision and that macOS stays unmeasured until a runner is approved.

The ROADMAP keeps the three re-add options (A on verify, B nightly schedule, C push-to-main) with recommendation B, and notes explicitly that adopting any of them needs approval because it partly reverses the 2026-09-05 owner decision.

What EPIC-115 did deliver is the correction: README.md's platform table now reads macOS 'not currently measured' with no 'how' column, replacing a false claim that macOS was verified on every pull request; the same table had also wrongly said Windows ran only on push to main.

The gap the record names is ongoing coverage, not knowledge: the unmeasured behaviours are the POSIX global-install path and the shutdown contract (seven signal tests skip on Windows because Node delivers no SIGTERM there).
Nothing after 2026-09-05 reversed the reversal; later macOS mentions (e.g. commit 2267e28) correct benchmark fixtures that had recorded the pre-reversal arrangement.

AC-2 was restated during implementation: 'never exceeds its *requested* budget' is unachievable because fixed fields cost ~470 tokens, so a request below MIN_BUDGET (800) is raised and told so and the promise is `estimatedTokens <= budget as reported`. AC-6 requires re-running `benchmark/` and `benchmark/agent/` and recording the movement, explicitly stating 'A number moving against Ferret here is the fix working' and that the benchmarks are not adjusted to compensate. The Definition of Done also requires an after column in docs/evidence/FERRET-DOES-A-REAL-AGENT-DO-BETTER.md §5 and Corrections sections in both benchmarks.

The re-runs appear already executed but uncommitted: untracked benchmark/agent/results/delivery-after.json, benchmark/continuity/results/after-epic-136.json, benchmark/results/before-epic-136.json, plus modified benchmark/results/latest.json and the two continuity notes files.

The headline Phase 5 result must not be overstated: commit 0a66a88 is titled 'does a real agent do better work with Ferret? Measured, and no'. EPIC-136 §2 records the treatment arm reading 2.9 files/355 lines against the control's 6.1/807 yet spending 433 908 tokens a task against 417 075, with cached input 268 125 against 156 273 (72% more) from thirty tool definitions re-sent every turn.

scripts/dogfood.mjs writes four wordings as durable context on every run — including 'Ferret dogfoods itself through a surface no agent uses', which exists only to test that normalization does *not* fold it into the other three — plus the candidate 'A proposal is not a belief until somebody accepts it'. ferret_context_find returns these as active facts with no supersedes edge, and ferret_context_trust reports the three-observation record as 'current, but nothing in the evidence distinguishes the observations behind it'.

The only durable record in the store that is a genuine project decision is 47a0bfcd: 'Durable context is reachable through ferret_search only when kinds is restricted to context; the fix for that was the tool description, not the default ranking' — matching commit 144d478 (#226).

scripts/dogfood.mjs is an oracle, not a demo: every question is answered independently from git, and every question goes through the MCP surface because 'a defect that only SQL can see is not a defect a client will ever hit'. EPIC-136 §8 requires its regression tests to go through the MCP surface for the same reason — §2.1 is invisible from the pack object and only appears once the response is serialized.

The durable-context dogfood checks skip rather than fail when the principal lacks `record`; EPIC-134 records that 'a check that quietly did not run reads exactly like one that passed', so skips are counted and named separately.

The principal a session runs as changes what it can see: this session (benchmark.agent.reader) is refused `mcp.config.exclusions` for want of `config.read`, and the benchmark harness and evidence reports (docs/evidence/FERRET-DOES-A-REAL-AGENT-DO-BETTER.md, benchmark/continuity/results/notes-*.md) are excluded from its corpus.

The pack budget defect had already been fixed once at a different site: commit 911745d (#215) fixed the per-item under-count; 68033a7 fixes the envelope. EPIC-136 §2.1 names them as the same defect class, so #215 must not be read as having already covered this.
